Does this geometry carry an independent identifier, or is it identified only through its host binding, role and version?
Which Spatial Thing does this geometry represent, and is that thing recorded as distinct from the geometry object itself?
What binding role and cardinality apply - is this the default geometry, an alternative representation, or a derived generalization?
If content-derived identity is used, which canonical form and digest algorithm produce it, and is it treated as a deduplication handle rather than a public identifier?
Which event time and which observation or ingestion time apply to this geometry value, separately from the host's own validity period?
Which resolvable CRS identifier is bound to this geometry, and which authority resolves it?
In which axis order are the coordinate tuples stored, and does that order follow the referenced coordinate system axes or an overriding delivery convention?
If the referenced CRS is dynamic, which coordinate epoch do these coordinates belong to?
When no CRS reference is present, which default applies, and is that default asserted in the record or merely assumed by the consumer?
If these coordinates resulted from a coordinate transformation, which operation was referenced and what positional-quality statement accompanies the result?
Which primitive class does this geometry belong to - point, curve or surface - and which concrete type name expresses it?
Which interpolation rule connects consecutive positions along a curve or a surface boundary?
Is a self-intersecting curve permitted here, and is a closed curve treated as a ring or merely as a closed line?
Which of these primitive types survive projection into the target encoding profile, and which degrade or fail?
Is this value a homogeneous multipart aggregate or a heterogeneous geometry collection, and which part types does it admit?
Are nested collections permitted, and if so to what depth?
Are individual parts separately addressable, and is part order semantically meaningful or incidental?
Must the parts be mutually disjoint or non-overlapping, and which party asserts that condition?
Is a single-part aggregate normalized to a bare primitive, and does that normalization change the recorded type?
What are the topological dimension, coordinate dimension and spatial dimension of this geometry, and do they agree with its declared type?
Is the third ordinate a spatial Z value or a non-spatial measure, and against which vertical reference is Z interpreted?
Must Z and M be present on every position of the value, or may they be partially populated?
What measure semantics and unit apply to the M ordinate, and who defines them?
How are Z and M carried, dropped or defaulted when the value is projected into an encoding that does not support them?
What is the minimum number of positions required for the declared geometry type, and does this value meet it?
What ordinate precision is stored and what spatial resolution is declared, and are these kept distinct from positional accuracy?
Are repeated consecutive positions permitted in the sequence, and how are they treated on validation and canonicalization?
Which encoding projection carried this coordinate sequence, and is that projection lossless for the declared ordinate set and precision?
Is ring closure represented by an explicit repeated final position, or implied by the encoding rules?
Which orientation convention applies to exterior and interior rings, and is that convention normative for this value or only a property of the delivery encoding?
How is each interior ring associated with its exterior ring, and may holes be nested, touch the exterior, or split the interior?
Does a reversed or unclosed ring make the geometry invalid, or merely non-canonical and subject to normalization?
Is the geometry empty with a retained type, absent from the host binding, unknown, or deliberately suppressed?
Does an empty geometry retain its declared type, CRS binding and ordinate declarations?
How are sentinel or placeholder coordinates prevented from being read as a real position?
Where location is generalized or withheld for privacy, safety or security reasons, is that recorded as suppression rather than as absence?
Is the recorded extent an envelope in the geometry's own CRS or a bounding box expressed in a separate delivery CRS?
How is an extent that crosses the antimeridian encoded, and how is a pole-containing extent expressed?
Was the extent computed from the coordinates, declared independently, or inherited from a parent collection?
Is the extent guaranteed to contain the geometry, or is it an approximation subject to a stated tolerance?
Which derived summary point is recorded - a mathematical centroid or a guaranteed interior representative point - and can it fall outside the geometry?
Against which named validity profile and version was this geometry assessed, and what verdict was returned?
Which evaluator produced the verdict, and is the verdict held here only as a reference to that external assessment?
What tolerance or snapping distance was applied when assessing coincident and near-coincident positions?
If the geometry was repaired or normalized, what changed and which prior value does the current one supersede?
At what observation time was validity last assessed, and does that assessment still apply to the current coordinate payload?
Which relation family and predicate name is asserted between the two geometry values?
Under which CRS, dimensionality and tolerance was the relation asserted?
Is the relation an asserted fact of record, or a cached result of an external evaluation that may be recomputed and invalidated?
Do the two related geometries share a CRS binding, and if not, how is that mismatch declared rather than silently resolved?
Are edges interpreted as straight lines in the CRS coordinate space or as geodesics on the reference ellipsoid?
How does this geometry cross or avoid the antimeridian - by being cut into parts, by longitude values outside the normal range, or by a spherical interpretation?
Does the geometry enclose, touch or approach a pole, and which convention expresses that region?
Which interpretation prevails when the encoding profile's convention and the declared edge rule disagree?
Does the geometry use curved segments, a patch-based surface, or a volumetric solid beyond the linear simple-feature types?
For a solid, how are its bounding shells declared, and must each shell be closed and consistently orientable?
Which validity rules apply to non-planar surfaces and solids, given that planar simple-feature assertions do not fully cover them?
What fallback or linearized representation is offered to consumers that cannot process curved or volumetric geometry, and at what tolerance?
Which authority issued the identifier of record for this CRS, and what exact code did it issue?
Is the cited authority the custodian that governs this definition, or a downstream mirror or vendor catalogue?
In what resolvable URI form is the identifier expressed for exchange, and does that URI carry a real registry version or the wildcard token?
What rule forbids treating a bare code, a projection nickname or a vendor string as sufficient identification here?
Which secondary identifiers describe the same CRS, and which one prevails when they disagree?
Which registry release and which retrieval event produced the definition currently held for this CRS?
How is the observation time of the snapshot kept separate from the authority's own publication and revision dates?
What integrity evidence proves the held snapshot has not drifted from the authority record?
Who may re-pin the snapshot, how long is the superseded pin kept, and what remains after it is reduced?
What is recorded when the registry is unreachable and only a cached definition is available?
Is the CRS carried by reference only, by full definition, or both, and what drove that choice?
When both a reference and a full definition are present, which one prevails and how is divergence detected?
Which elements must a carried definition contain before it can be used without contacting the registry?
Which version of the exchange form is declared, so that a consumer parses the carried definition against the right grammar?
What metadata is known to be absent when a definition travels as a well-known text string rather than as a registry record?
What is the authority's official name for this CRS, and how does it differ from the label shown to users?
Which recorded strings are authority aliases, which are legacy or vendor labels, and which are unclassified?
What rule prevents any name, alias or label from being resolved back to a definition on its own?
Do two distinct CRS records share a name or alias here, and how is that ambiguity resolved?
What validity status does the authority currently assign to this CRS record?
Which record supersedes this one, and is the supersession a correction, a re-realization or a policy replacement?
From when is the deprecation effective, and how does that relate to data already captured in the deprecated CRS?
Under what conditions may a deprecated CRS still be referenced, and who approves that?
Which national or regional modernization programme drives this supersession, and what coordinate change does it imply?
Which datum or reference frame does this CRS use, and by what authority code is that frame identified?
Is the referenced frame a single named realization, a datum ensemble, or a dynamic reference frame?
If the frame is dynamic, what is its frame reference epoch and what coordinate epoch applies to the coordinates themselves?
What comparability limit follows from citing an ensemble instead of a named realization?
Which global or plate-fixed frame is this datum aligned to, and at what epoch was that alignment made?
Which ellipsoid parameters define the reference surface, and in which length unit are they expressed?
Which prime meridian does the CRS use, and what is its longitude offset from Greenwich?
How is it verified that these constants match the authority record rather than an implementation default?
What is recorded when a CRS uses a non-Greenwich prime meridian or a spherical approximation?
Which coordinate system type does this CRS use, and how many axes does it declare?
For each axis, what are its name, abbreviation, direction, unit of measure and declared range?
What is the authority-defined position of each axis in the coordinate tuple, and in which element was that order read explicitly?
Where a serialization or interface imposes its own axis order, how is the divergence from the authority order recorded and reconciled?
What evidence shows that a producing system's tuple length and axis order actually match the authority definition?
Which CRS subtype does this definition instantiate, and which element states it?
For a projected or derived CRS, which base CRS and which defining conversion does it reference?
For a compound CRS, which component CRS are combined, in which order, and what does each contribute?
For a vertical or engineering CRS, what is the height or local reference and what must not be assumed about it?
When a subject needs horizontal and vertical position together, is a compound CRS or two separate references used, and why?
What scope does the authority state for this CRS, and does the intended use fall inside it?
What is the declared domain of validity, and in which CRS is the bounding box itself expressed?
What follows when coordinates fall outside the declared domain of validity?
Which CRS are permitted for a given subject or collection, and who approved that list?
How is the applicability profile expressed so a consumer knows which CRS it may ask for?
Is the underlying reference frame static, plate-fixed or dynamic, and which defining clause or register attribute establishes that?
What frame reference epoch defines this dynamic reference frame, and in which notation is it expressed?
Which authority defines and publishes this frame realization, under which document and at which version?
What evidence justifies treating the frame as static for the subject's stated positional tolerance?
Is a coordinate epoch required for this coordinate set, and which rule or policy makes it required?
At which scope is the coordinate epoch bound — dataset, layer, feature or individual coordinate tuple?
Which coordinate epoch value applies to these coordinates, in decimal year and as an RFC 3339 instant?
What disposition is recorded when a dynamic reference is used but no coordinate epoch can be established?
Which carrier field conveys the coordinate epoch in the chosen encoding, and what is lost if the carrier is absent?
Which distinct time roles are recorded for this coordinate set, and how is each one defined?
Does the observation time of these coordinates differ from their coordinate epoch, and what reconciled them?
When was the cited reference or deformation-model definition published, and when was this record ingested?
Which validation prevents a coordinate epoch from being stored or interpreted as a record creation timestamp?
Does this coordinate reference resolve to a datum ensemble or to a single named realization member?
What ensemble accuracy is published for this ensemble, and does it satisfy the subject's positional tolerance?
Which realization members belong to the ensemble, and which member actually produced these coordinates?
Under which constraint is ensemble-level referencing prohibited for this subject?
Which deformation or point-motion model, at which published version, governs epoch propagation for this reference?
What spatial and temporal extent bounds the cited deformation model's declared validity?
Which authority publishes, versions and evaluates the cited deformation model?
What is recorded when the subject location or required epoch falls outside the cited model's declared extent?
What is the temporal datum origin of this axis, and in which calendar is it expressed?
Which time scale does the temporal axis realize, and which authority maintains that scale?
Is the temporal axis a date-time, a temporal count or a temporal measure, and what unit does it use?
How are leap seconds and the decided future change to the maximum UT1-UTC difference handled on this axis?
Which vertical reference frame do these heights or depths refer to?
Is the vertical reference frame static or dynamic, and does it carry its own frame reference epoch distinct from the horizontal frame?
Through which geoid or geopotential model version is the vertical frame realized?
Is the vertical axis a height with up positive or a depth with down positive, and in what unit?
Which component coordinate references make up this compound reference?
In which order are the components declared, and what axis sequence and units result from that order?
What evidence shows the components are independent, as a compound reference requires?
If any component is dynamic, does the coordinate epoch apply to that component alone or to the whole compound reference?
How is the compound reference degraded or rejected when a consumer supports only one component?
Is this reference unknown, custom, engineering-local, or a deprecated or superseded register entry?
Does this reference carry a resolvable definition or a complete governed snapshot sufficient to interpret coordinates without external lookup?
For an engineering or local reference, which anchor point, orientation and carrier object define it, and does that carrier move?
Which state is recorded when a definition cannot be resolved, and which uses are then prohibited?
Who may register, amend or approve a custom definition for the adopting Dimension?
Which register authority, register version and code identify the definition in force for these coordinates?
Which canonical form and integrity value fix the pinned definition text against silent drift?
How is a pinned snapshot marked when the register later deprecates or supersedes the entry?
How long must a pinned snapshot be retained relative to the coordinates that cite it, and who executes disposal?
Which governed identifier names the source coordinate reference system and which names the target?
Is each coordinate reference system carried by resolvable reference rather than as a locally redefined description?
From which registry authority and dataset version were the endpoint definitions taken?
Does any step require an interpolation coordinate reference system distinct from its source and target?
To which coordinate epoch are the input coordinates referenced, and to which epoch are the output coordinates referenced?

Is a point-motion or deformation step required to move coordinates between the source and target epochs?
What outcome is recorded when a dynamic reference system is in use and no coordinate epoch is supplied?
What area of use bounds each step of the chain, and does the subject geometry lie inside it?
Which spatial test governed selection: strict containment of the area of interest or mere intersection?
Is the selected chain a ballpark, null or copy operation whose accuracy is unknown?
What outcome is recorded when coordinates fall outside the declared area of use?
Is each step a conversion, a transformation, a point-motion operation or a pure axis and unit change?
Do the source and target of a step share the same datum, making that step a conversion rather than a transformation?
Is the chain a single operation or a concatenated operation, and which constituent operations form it?
Which registry-held definition does each step cite, and was that definition current or superseded when pinned?
Which operation method identifier and version pin each step of the chain?
Are all method parameter values recorded with explicit units and no implied or engine-defaulted values?
In what order are the steps applied, and which of them are applied in the inverse direction?
Which operation version label identifies the parameter set, so that the same chain can be rebuilt later?
Which grid, triangulated-network or deformation-model resources does the chain require, and how is each identified and versioned?
What integrity value binds this record to the exact resource content that was used?
What outcome is recorded when a required resource is unavailable at evaluation time?
Which transformation engine version and registry dataset version were in force when the result was produced?
Which original geometry and original coordinate reference system does this derived geometry come from?
Which representation is authoritative when the original and a derived geometry disagree?
When was the derived geometry produced, and is that time kept separate from the time the geometry itself was valid?
Is the recorded lineage sufficient to reproduce the derived geometry from the original?
What accuracy value does the defining authority state for each step, and in what unit?
How is a single accuracy figure derived for the whole chain from its per-step values?
Which authority stated the accuracy, and is it a published statement rather than a local estimate?
Is chain accuracy marked unknown whenever any step lacks a published accuracy or is a fallback?
What positional uncertainty is attached to the output coordinates, split into horizontal and vertical components?
At what confidence level and by what evaluation method is the uncertainty expressed?
Does the uncertainty come from a per-point local error estimate or from a single blanket figure for the whole operation?
What stored numeric precision and coordinate resolution are used, and is stored precision coarser than the stated uncertainty?
In which axis order are the coordinates written, and does that order come from the CRS definition or from an encoding rule?
Which unit applies to each ordinate, and were units normalized before the operation was applied?
Does the chain change coordinate dimensionality, for example dropping a height ordinate or adding a time ordinate?
What outcome is recorded when the input dimensionality is not supported by a step of the chain?
Was the geometry densified before the operation, and to what deviation tolerance?
How was a geometry crossing the antimeridian treated, and was it split rather than left spanning?
Was any clipping or longitude wrapping applied, and what extent governed it?
How is behaviour near the poles and near projection singularities declared?
What single outcome status does the record carry for the applied chain as a whole?
Which named exception applies: missing resource, out-of-area, epoch mismatch, axis ambiguity, unsupported dimension, invalid geometry, tolerance breach or lossy export?
Which declared tolerance was tested against the result, and did the result breach it?
Is any round-trip claim limited to chains that are bijective, non-iterative and unrounded?
What must a consumer be told before treating the derived geometry as fit for its purpose?
Which named party holds each accountable role for this geometry and coordinate-reference attachment?
Are the recorded role assignments advisory attributes rather than access grants?
How is the independent reviewer kept distinct from the producer and the approver of the same attachment?
What applies when a role is vacant, delegated, or the host object changes owner?
Which role covers the case where the geodetic authority sits outside the adopting organisation?
Who is authorised to select or change the coordinate reference system bound to this host object?
Which decision record justifies the chosen CRS, transformation path and grid?
Does a coordinate correction proceed as an in-place correction or as a new approved version?
Which transformation methods, grids and minimum accuracy are permitted for this subject?
What escalation applies when the geodetic authority deprecates or replaces a referenced definition?
What identifier distinguishes this attachment from other geometry attachments on the same host object?
Does an authoritative master-system identifier already exist for this geometry, and is it recorded?
How is the coordinate reference system cited so that the citation stays unambiguous and resolvable?
Does attachment identity survive host-object merge, split or re-identification?
Which version of this attachment is current, and which are retained but no longer current?
Over what effective interval is this version asserted to hold?
Which prior version does this record supersede and on what stated ground?
How is a deprecated or retired CRS definition handled without breaking existing citations?
What distinguishes a non-substantive correction from a change that requires a new version?
Which source geometry, survey or dataset was this geometry derived from?
Which definition version, coordinate operation and grid file were used to produce the current values?
When was the geometry observed or surveyed, and when was it captured into this record?
Which agent, software version and parameter set performed the derivation?
What residual positional uncertainty is asserted for the derived geometry?
What evidence shows an independent reviewer examined this geometry and its coordinate-reference binding?
Which checks must pass before release, and which are advisory only?
Who approved release of this version and under what authority basis?
How are rejection and conditional approval recorded and resubmitted?
On what basis is this location classified as sensitive, and which party determined it?
Which generalization method applies, and what precision is released compared with the precision retained?
How is the fact and degree of generalization disclosed to downstream consumers?
When is the sensitivity classification reviewed again, and what triggers an earlier review?
Which recipients may receive full precision, and which component decides that?
Under which licence is each input held - CRS definition, transformation grid and source geometry?
May the derived geometry be redistributed, and under what conditions?
Which attribution or acknowledgement notices must accompany a published copy?
Does the ability to read a grid, definition or source geometry imply any right to redistribute it?
What retention class applies to this attachment and to its supporting evidence records?
Is this record under a hold that suspends disposition, and who imposed it?
What remains visible after removal, and what does the tombstone assert?
Which component executes destruction or transfer, and on whose authority?
What happens to the attachment when the host object is retired or transferred?
Which interoperability profile or encoding contract does this attachment declare?
Is the declaration an alignment statement or an evidenced conformance claim?
Which externally held audit, decision or registry records does this attachment point to?
How is a conflict between two declared external specifications recorded?
Which instant governs this read: the event time the geometry is asserted to describe, or the observation time at which the record became known?
Is the resolved reference frame dynamic, and if so which coordinate epoch qualifies the returned coordinates?
Which registry release was in force for the resolved context, and what was the status of the referenced code at that release?
Which authorization reference accompanied the read, and which external decision reference was returned for it?
What is reported when no context version is in force at the requested instant?
Which identifier binds this geometry and coordinate reference context to its host, and which authority issued that identifier?
What role does this geometry play for the host, and how many geometries of that role may coexist?
Which kind of coordinate reference system is bound, and is its datum a single realization or an ensemble?
Which coordinate reference system is declared as the storage CRS for this binding, and which others may it be served in?
Which idempotency key scopes a repeated create or correction request, and over what window must the same key yield the same reported outcome?
Which version precondition must a mutating request carry so that a stale write is rejected rather than merged?
Which authorization reference and policy reference must accompany the request, and which external point returns the decision?
Which distinct failure codes are emitted for an unresolvable CRS, a missing coordinate epoch, an unavailable transformation resource, a precondition mismatch and a hold conflict?
Which states may a geometry and coordinate reference context version occupy between issue and supersession?
Which prior version does this correction supersede, and what reason and evidence justify it?
Which host references and derived geometries must be re-pointed or re-derived once this version is superseded?
Which classes of change require a new version rather than an annotation on the existing one?
Which retention rule governs disposition of this binding, and where is the governing policy defined?
Is a legal or regulatory hold asserted against this binding, and by which reference?
Which incoming references would break on destruction, and what minimal residual payload must survive as a tombstone?
Which coordinate precision or locational attributes must be removed or generalised before any residual record is kept?

Which coordinate reference context fields are mandatory before publication, and which become mandatory only for a dynamic reference frame?
Do the declared axis units, axis order and coordinate dimension agree with the actual coordinate tuples?
Does the geometry fall within the stated area of validity of the referenced CRS and of any pinned operation?
Which validation severities are distinguished, and which of them block publication rather than warn?
Which coordinate operation is pinned for this transformation, and which candidate operations were considered and rejected?
Which engine, registry release and transformation resources must be recorded so that the result can be re-derived exactly?

When the two operands carry different coordinate epochs, at which epoch is the comparison performed?
Does equality of the two CRS references actually establish equality of realization, or is one of them a datum ensemble?
What is reported when comparability fails, and may a result ever be returned with a qualification instead?
Which target binding is requested, and which parts of the coordinate reference context can that binding not carry?
Which specific losses occurred on this export, and what is the magnitude of each?
Which redaction or coordinate generalisation was applied before export, and under which reference?
Which loss classes must block an export rather than merely be reported?

requirements: Run a separate no-tools adversarial audit of the active provider result.
Verify the model boundary and entry kind against the frozen relationship contract.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Expose the owner-authorized provider waiver in every publication artifact.
Keep the result reviewable-draft while independent second-provider review is waived.
